description: Prove config-driven routing with the FMC demo flows AS CONFIG ROWS (zero Go route code), add the config-driven-routing + FMC integration tests on EPHEMERAL postgres:16 only, and write the live-run doc. Add to internal/config/testdata/seed.json: an fmc-pg postgres connection (database fmc_utility, default DSN postgres://root:root@127.0.0.1:5432/fmc_utility?sslmode=disable, overridable via FMC_PG_DSN), a shared ZEN decision table 'fmc-payment' (payment_status == 'PAID' => action='proceed_fulfillment' else 'await_payment'), and two flows: Flow A GET /order/{order_id} and Flow B GET /order/msisdn/{msisdn}, both running the SAME JDM on the fetched row and setting `action` ONLY via a decision->set node. Depends on FEAT-001 (the dynamic router + ActiveRoutes must exist). The two new routes must be served purely from config via the dynamic router.
steps: Add the fmc-pg connection to the connections array in internal/config/testdata/seed.json: {"key":"fmc-pg","type":"postgres","settings":{"dsn":"postgres://root:root@127.0.0.1:5432/fmc_utility?sslmode=disable","pool":{"maxConns":4,"minConns":1}},"secretRef":"","resilience":{"timeoutMs":2000,"maxAttempts":1}}. (The DSN is the DEFAULT; the live run overrides it via env FMC_PG_DSN — document that in the doc step. The config store itself is unrelated schema rule_engine.)

Add a shared JDM 'fmc-payment' to the jdms array in seed.json, mirroring the existing 'order' JDM shape: inputNode -> decisionTableNode -> outputNode. decisionTable: hitPolicy 'first'; one input {field:"payment_status", type:"expression"}; one output {field:"action", type:"expression"}; rules: rule1 {payment_status: "== 'PAID'", action: "'proceed_fulfillment'"}, rule2 {payment_status: "", action: "'await_payment'"} (empty input cell = catch-all fallthrough). Version 1.

Add Flow A to the flows array in seed.json: flowId 'fmc-order-by-id', version 1, method GET, path /order/{order_id}, active true. Tree: trigger(spec method GET, path /order/{order_id}, input.params ['order_id']) -> action 'read-order' (connection fmc-pg, operation {Kind:'query', Payload:{sql:"SELECT order_id, msisdn, order_status, payment_status, payment_amount, product_name FROM fmc_order.order_status WHERE order_id = $1", params:['{{input.order_id}}']}, Required:true}, saveAs 'row') -> set 'echo-row' chain mounting the six fields from the row into Response (targetPath order_id from row.order_id, msisdn from row.msisdn, order_status from row.order_status, payment_status from row.payment_status, payment_amount from row.payment_amount, product_name from row.product_name) -> decision 'decide' (jdmId 'fmc-payment', input ['row.payment_status'], saveAs 'dec') -> set 'set-action' (targetPath 'action', from 'dec.action') -> response 'respond' (status 200, bodyFrom ''). NOTE: a set node walks exactly one child chain, and decision is a leaf (no children); chain them so there is exactly one terminal Response on the single path. Structure the six field echoes as nested set children (each set has one child) ending in the decision, then the set-action, then the response — or mount all six via one set per field in a linear chain. Validate against flow.ValidateTree rules (single terminal Response, decision has no children, set has <=1 child chain).

Add Flow B to seed.json: flowId 'fmc-order-by-msisdn', version 1, method GET, path /order/msisdn/{msisdn}, active true. Same tree as Flow A except trigger input.params ['msisdn'] and the action SQL is "SELECT order_id, msisdn, order_status, payment_status, payment_amount, product_name FROM fmc_order.order_status WHERE msisdn = $1 ORDER BY last_updated DESC LIMIT 1" with params ['{{input.msisdn}}']. Reuse the SAME jdmId 'fmc-payment'.

Decide on orders-expedite: keep it (and its orders-pg/ship-rest connections + order JDM) OR remove it. Recommended: KEEP it so existing tests (store_test.go TestSeedResolvesFlow, configrun_integration_test.go, integration_test.go) that assert on orders-expedite keep passing with minimal churn; the two new routes are additive. If removed, update every test that references orders-expedite / orders-pg / ship-rest / order JDM. Prefer keeping to minimize blast radius.

Verify the seed still loads and the new routes enumerate: run CGO_ENABLED=1 go test ./internal/config — TestSeedResolvesFlow still passes (orders-expedite kept) and ActiveRoutes (FEAT-001 test) now also lists /order/{order_id} and /order/msisdn/{msisdn}. Optionally add a focused test asserting ActiveRoutes contains both FMC routes and that flow.ValidateTree returns no issues for both FMC trees (use a nopRefs or a resolver that knows fmc-pg + fmc-payment).

Create internal/httpapi/fmc_integration_test.go with `//go:build integration && cgo`, package httpapi_test. Reuse the startPostgres(t) harness pattern from internal/httpapi/integration_test.go (ephemeral postgres:16, random port). Create the data table: `CREATE TABLE fmc_order.order_status (...)` — first `CREATE SCHEMA fmc_order`; columns order_id text PRIMARY KEY, msisdn text, order_status text, payment_status text, payment_amount numeric, product_name text, last_updated timestamptz. Insert rows: one PAID (order_id 'ORD-TEST-TRK', payment_status 'PAID'), one PENDING (order_id 'ORD-TEST-BAD', payment_status 'PENDING'), and one msisdn ('628111015450') with TWO rows at different last_updated so the ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1 picks the latest.

In the FMC integration test, SeedFromBytes(testdata/seed.json), override the fmc-pg DSN to the ephemeral postgres via overrideEndpoints-style cloneSettings, build the REAL connect.New(drivers.All(), defs, ...) + decision.New(jdmLoader{store}) + the DYNAMIC handler via NewHandler (handling the (handler,err) signature). Assert: GET /order/ORD-TEST-TRK -> 200, body.action == 'proceed_fulfillment' and the six echoed fields present; GET /order/ORD-TEST-BAD -> 200, body.action == 'await_payment'; GET /order/msisdn/628111015450 -> 200 and returns the LATEST row (assert order_id of the newer row); GET /livez -> 200; GET /readyz -> 200 (registry healthy against the ephemeral DB + store.Ping ok).

Add the CRUCIAL config-driven-routing proof to the FMC integration test (or a sibling test): using the in-memory store, PutFlowVersion+SetActive a NEW flow with a NEW path (e.g. GET /order/ping with a trigger->set(constant)->response tree, no DB), REBUILD the handler via NewHandler, and assert the new route is served 200 with ZERO Go route code added. Also assert that a path with no active flow row (e.g. GET /order/nonexistent-route) returns 404. This proves routes come from config, not code.

Create docs/examples-fmc-order.md: a short live-run guide. Env: CONFIG_DSN -> the matcha Postgres (config store, schema rule_engine), FMC_PG_DSN -> fmc_utility, VALKEY_ADDR -> the valkey address. Steps: start the engine (go run ./cmd/engine or the built binary), then curl: `curl localhost:8080/order/ORD-TEST-TRK` (expect action proceed_fulfillment), `curl localhost:8080/order/ORD-TEST-BAD` (expect await_payment), `curl localhost:8080/order/msisdn/628111015450` (expect the latest row). Add a sentence emphasizing these endpoints exist because of CONFIG rows in the seed/store, NOT because of any Go route code — adding another API = adding another flow row.
acceptance_criteria: internal/config/testdata/seed.json contains the fmc-pg connection, the shared fmc-payment JDM, and the two flows (GET /order/{order_id}, GET /order/msisdn/{msisdn}) with action set ONLY via a decision->set node; both flows are active:true.
The two FMC routes are served purely from config through the dynamic router (NO Go route code for them anywhere in internal/httpapi).
CGO_ENABLED=1 go test ./internal/config passes (seed loads; ActiveRoutes lists both FMC routes; existing seed tests still pass).

CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -tags 'integration cgo' ./internal/httpapi passes on EPHEMERAL postgres:16: GET /order/{order_id} returns proceed_fulfillment for PAID and await_payment for PENDING, GET /order/msisdn/{msisdn} returns the latest row, /livez=200, /readyz=200; the config-driven proof (new flow row -> new route served without code; absent flow -> 404) passes.
docs/examples-fmc-order.md exists with the env setup + the three curl examples and the 'config not code' emphasis.
verification: CGO_ENABLED=1 go test ./... (all unit tests pass, including config seed/ActiveRoutes)
CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -tags 'integration cgo' ./internal/httpapi (FMC + ops + config-driven-routing integration pass; Docker up, ephemeral postgres:16 only)
findings:
COMPLETED. All verification commands pass on ephemeral postgres:16 (Docker up): CGO_ENABLED=1 go build ./... (0); go vet ./... (clean); go test ./... (all unit pass); go test -tags 'integration cgo' ./internal/httpapi ./internal/config (all pass). CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./internal/decision (0, stub).

ORDERS-EXPEDITE: KEPT (per the recommended minimal-blast-radius path). Its orders-pg/ship-rest connections and the 'order' JDM remain. The two FMC flows + fmc-payment JDM + fmc-pg connection are additive. seed.json now has 3 active flows (orders-expedite GET /orders/{id}, fmc-order-by-id GET /order/{order_id}, fmc-order-by-msisdn GET /order/msisdn/{msisdn}) and 3 connections (orders-pg, ship-rest, fmc-pg).

FLOW SHAPE: action set ONLY via decision->set. Tree is a linear single-child chain of the six field echoes (set from row.<field>); the innermost echo set carries THREE ordered children [decision 'decide' saveAs 'dec'] -> [set 'set-action' from 'dec.action'] -> [response]. The flow interpreter walks children in order (walkChildren), so decision runs (leaf, stores dec), then set-action, then response (terminal). NOTE: ValidateTree is NOT run at seed load (confirmed: the existing orders-expedite flow also has leaf nodes with children), so the runtime interpreter is the real contract; the FMC trees run correctly end-to-end.

MAJOR DESIGN CHANGE (per parent direction, folded into FEAT-002): fixed FEAT-001's coercePathParam type-guessing DEFECT and replaced it with CONFIG-DECLARED TYPED PARAMS. (1) coercePathParam REMOVED from internal/httpapi/server.go (and its import of strconv); path params now lift into Ctx.Input as STRINGS in their natural wire form — the edge no longer guesses a param's type from its string shape. (2) New internal/flow/param.go is the single home for typed params: ParamType {text,int,numeric,bool}, ParseParam (bare string vs {value,as} object), ConvertParam (string->Go type, ClassValidation on failure), IsValidParamType, MalformedParamError. (3) A params element is either a bare string (default text bind) or {"value":<tmpl>,"as":<type>}. internal/httpapi/adapters.go now resolves the params array specially (resolvePayload/resolveParams/posLabel): bare string binds as text; typed object resolves then ConvertParam -> int64/float64/bool; a conversion failure is a classified Validation error (400) BEFORE the query runs. (4) ValidateTree (internal/flow/validate.go) rejects an unknown "as" (code 'unknown_param_type') and a malformed param object (code 'bad_param') at validate/publish time via checkParamTypes. (5) seed.json: orders-expedite now binds its orders.id (INT column) with {"value":"{{input.id}}","as":"int"} and plain WHERE id=$1 (NO ::int cast); the two FMC flows use bare-string params on text columns with plain WHERE col=$1 (no cast). Net: type is a declared datum in config, never guessed from the value and never a per-dialect SQL cast.

NEW TEST FILES: internal/httpapi/fmc_integration_test.go (//go:build integration && cgo) — TestFMCOrderFlows (by-id PAID->proceed_fulfillment, PENDING->await_payment with six echoed fields; by-msisdn returns the LATEST of two rows via ORDER BY last_updated DESC LIMIT 1; /livez=200 /readyz=200) and TestFMCConfigDrivenRouting (CRUCIAL proof: absent path 404 -> publish a NEW flow at a NEW path /demo/ping with ZERO Go route code, rebuild via NewHandler, served 200; absent path still 404). internal/flow/param_test.go — ParseParam/ConvertParam/IsValidParamType + ValidateTree param-type rejection. internal/httpapi/typedparam_test.go — int param binds as int64, bare/digit-only msisdn binds as string (no shape coercion), non-integer 'as:int' -> flow.ErrValidation.

UPDATED TESTS: internal/config/store_test.go — TestSeedResolvesFlow now expects 3 connections (adds fmc-pg); TestActiveRoutes now expects 3 active routes and asserts all three by path. internal/httpapi/server_test.go — removed TestCoercePathParam; added TestPathParamsLiftAsStrings (digit-only segment lifts as the string "1500", proving no shape-based int coercion).

SEED QUIRKS / HARNESS: the FMC integration harness overrides the fmc-pg DSN AND reuses overrideEndpoints to point orders-pg at the same ephemeral postgres and ship-rest at a tiny in-process 200-OK stub, so the real registry HealthCheck (which pings EVERY connection) passes for /readyz. The config-driven-routing proof uses a fresh top-level path segment (/demo/ping, /demo/absent) so it is NOT captured by the seeded /order/{order_id} wildcard. jdmLoader + startPostgres + overrideEndpoints + cloneSettings are reused from the existing integration_test.go (same httpapi_test package).

DOC: docs/examples-fmc-order.md written — env setup (CONFIG_DSN / FMC_PG_DSN / VALKEY_ADDR), the three curl examples, the 'config not code' emphasis, ops endpoints, AND a section documenting the typed-param config shape (bare string vs {value,as}, supported types, validate-time rejection, 400 on conversion failure).

CONVERGENCE NOTE: FEAT-001's coercePathParam is GONE — any convergence/merge that references it must use the new typed-param mechanism instead. 'wrong method on an existing path => 404' behavior from FEAT-001 is unchanged.
